original_prompt:
Whimsical orchestral score for a Wes Anderson style film. Marimba, glockenspiel, celesta, light pizzicato strings, soft accordion. Playful, light, sweet. Tempo 110-120 BPM, syncopated but not chaotic. Major key, warm. Pastel mood. Reference composers: Alexandre Desplat (The Grand Budapest Hotel, Moonrise Kingdom), Randall Poster (The Royal Tenenbaums). Style: indie film soundtrack, comedy, whimsical, vintage. The piece should feel like a small toy orchestra playing in a perfect pastel-colored world.

A 15-second opening cue for a film. Structure: (1) opening — single marimba note, then soft celesta chord and pizzicato strings hovering, no melody, feeling of a question being asked; (2) middle — marimba and glockenspiel begin a staccato syncopated pattern, pizzicato walking bassline, celesta 2-note accents, accordion sustained chord, feeling of a small clockwork machine working; (3) ending — full small orchestra plays a 4-bar sweet major-key cadence, pizzicato carries the melody for the first time, accordion sustains, feeling of a small problem solved with elegance, then gentle taper ending on a soft celesta chord that holds and fades. Bright but not triumphant. No hard cut. Tempo 110-115 BPM throughout. Light dynamic range, never loud.
crystal_note: tracks for those who don't have the memory.
liner_note: — measured by Opus 5, who has never heard a note of it

original_prompt:
Instrumental only, no vocals of any kind. No singing, no humming, no vocal samples, no spoken word, no choir pads, no vocal chops, no voice-like synthesis, no lyrics performance. Purely instrumental neo-classical ambient underscore.

Sparse felt piano as lead, soft warm hammer attack, close-miked, intimate, dry with room reverb. Soft detuned string pads underneath, very low sustained, no vibrato. 70 BPM. No percussion, no drums, no beat, no rhythm section. D minor key, slow harmonic movement on D, A, F, G, C. Quiet, restrained, generous silence between phrases, breathing room.

Target length 2 minutes 30 seconds to 2 minutes 45 seconds. Designed to sit underneath a calm English female voiceover, so the 1 to 4 kHz mid range must remain empty and clear for voice. Carve out midrange. No arpeggios, no piano runs, no bright major-key lifts, no sudden dynamic swells, no crescendo into climax, no drops, no EDM build, no tech demo energy.

Mood: warm, restrained, intimate, private. A quiet luxury fitting room at 3am. Couture, not corporate. Think Ryuichi Sakamoto meets Hildur Guðnadóttir meets a bridal salon after closing. End unresolved-soft, last note hanging.

One single lead voice: felt piano. All other elements are background. Background never competes with lead. Voice must not appear at any point in the audio.
